review_notes: I read the whole file. It has six Prop-valued definitions, which are statements of Riemann inequality, index formula and Weil duality variants, plus two theorems proved by `linarith`. It has no `@[simp]` lemmas, no simp sets, no rewrite rules and no recursive definitions. So there is no existing simp rule that could loop, compete or expand unexpectedly. The definitions are propositions that get unfolded and applied through hypotheses, as in `hWD hω D`. Adding simp attributes to them would be unjustified. I grepped for uses elsewhere (the P2M/Sol files) and found no evidence that a simp interface is needed here. I did not inspect each downstream use in depth, so I am somewhat uncertain whether a simp lemma such as an `ell`/`indexOfSpecialty` rewrite is missing. Those declarations live in other files, not this one.
